objective_for_doctor:
Age: 31
Sex: M
Chief Complaint: facial weakness

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

I recently had a viral infection, and now I have facial weakness. I’m also having significant shortness of breath or difficulty breathing, and weakness in both my arms and/or both legs, with numbness or tingling in both arms and legs and around my mouth.
Did your weakness start in your feet and legs and progress upward toward your trunk and arms, or did it start in your face and move downward?
It started around my mouth with numbness/tingling and facial weakness, and then I also have weakness in both arms and/or both legs along with numbness/tingling in both arms and legs.
Are your deep tendon reflexes (like knee jerks or ankle jerks) diminished or absent, or are they normal/exaggerated?
I don't know.
Is the weakness symmetric (equal on both sides), and has it been rapidly progressing over hours, days, or weeks?
It feels symmetric, and it has been progressing over hours to days.
Have you experienced any loss of bladder or bowel control, or difficulty starting urination?
I don't know.

Do you have a distinct line or level on your body (like a band around your chest or waist) below which the numbness is present and above which sensation is normal, or is the numbness more diffuse without a clear boundary?
It feels more diffuse, without a clear boundary.
Is the facial weakness affecting both sides of your face equally, or is it only on one side?
It’s on both sides of my face equally.
Do you have double vision, drooping eyelids, or difficulty moving your eyes in any direction?
I don't know.
Have you had any diarrhea, loose stools, or gastrointestinal illness in the past 1-3 weeks?
I don't know.
Have you noticed any difficulty walking steadily or loss of balance/coordination, rather than just weakness?
I don’t know.
Have you had significant aching
I don’t know.
[DDX] Guillain-Barré syndrome (Acute Inflammatory Demyelinating Polyradiculoneuropathy), Miller Fisher syndrome, Acute transverse myelitis, Myasthenia gravis, Botulism
